claims.text: An alumina (Al2O3) coating on rollers and guide plates will reduce erosion by molten aluminum.
Reducing molten-aluminum erosion with an alumina coating will extend component service life.
Conventional metal components used in hot-dip aluminum plating are typically steel.
Conventional metal components are vulnerable to aluminum-induced corrosion and erosion during hot-dip processing.
A dense, well-bonded, high-purity alumina coating can be applied to critical equipment surfaces.
Pre-formed alumina refractory parts can be used in critical areas of hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
The alumina surface layer will remain stable and act as a diffusion barrier between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
The alumina layer is self-healing under the relevant high-temperature conditions.
Alumina is chemically inert toward liquid aluminum.
Alumina has a high melting point.
The inertness and high melting point of alumina diminish dissolution and erosion of the metal substrate.
Self-healing of the alumina coating may mitigate minor coating defects.
Alumina-coated components will have significantly lower corrosion and erosion rates than unprotected metal parts in molten aluminum.
Lower corrosion and erosion rates will produce longer component service life.
Coating defects, insufficient adhesion, thermal fatigue, or spallation during thermal-mechanical cycling may compromise protection.
The long-term durability of alumina coatings under cyclic hot-dip aluminum plating conditions has not been established and requires experimental validation.
